precepts.text: Sin committed by ignorance was atoned and forgiven, one law for him that is born among Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.
precepts.point: Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. Peter marks that spirit: they walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, despise government, presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Despising government, gossiping and murmuring against leadership, and refusing to gather with the body is that same dangerous spirit; the Lord said gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, and he works through spiritual men as he did through Moses and Aaron.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
Numbers 15 lays the two ways side by side, and this is the first, sin by ignorance: “if ought be committed by ignorance without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one young bullock for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour unto the Lord, with his meat offering, and his drink offering, according to the manner, and one kid of the goats for a sin offering. And the priest shall make an atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it shall be forgiven them; for it is ignorance”.

The same for one soul: “if any soul sin through ignorance, then he shall bring a she goat of the first year for a sin offering. And the priest shall make an atonement for the soul that sinneth ignorantly, when he sinneth by ignorance before the Lord, to make an atonement for him; and it shall be forgiven him.” That is the ruler’s kid of the goats in Leviticus 4: atonement made, reconciliation with the Lord, and forgiveness of sins.

“Ye shall have one law for him that sinneth through ignorance, both for him that is born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.” One law for the born Israelite and the stranger alike.

precepts.text: The soul that doeth ought presumptuously reproacheth the Lord and shall be cut off; he hath despised the word of the Lord.
precepts.point: Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. Peter marks that spirit: they walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, despise government, presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Despising government, gossiping and murmuring against leadership, and refusing to gather with the body is that same dangerous spirit; the Lord said gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, and he works through spiritual men as he did through Moses and Aaron.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
This is the other way, set right against the sin of ignorance: “the soul that doeth ought presumptuously, whether he be born in the land, or a stranger, the same reproacheth the Lord; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people. Because he hath despised the word of the Lord, and hath broken his commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off; his iniquity shall be upon him.”

There is no kid of the goats for this one. Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. He hath despised the word of the Lord, and his iniquity shall be upon him.

precepts.text: The man gathering sticks on the Sabbath was kept in ward until the mind of the Lord was declared, and the Lord said he shall surely be put to death.
precepts.point: That is the judgment on the willful: if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins. That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. The Lord knoweth all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts; he knoweth your inventions and what ye think in your heart, even them that sin and would hide their sin. Sin willfully and your grace period is up.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
The man found gathering sticks upon the Sabbath day shows the presumptuous side, immediately after that law was spoken. When they found him, “they that found him gathering sticks brought him unto Moses and Aaron, and unto all the congregation. And they put him in ward, because it was not declared what should be done to him.”

They did not kill him right away; they put him in ward, and Moses got direction from the Lord. “And the Lord said unto Moses, The man shall be surely put to death: all the congregation shall stone him with stones without the camp.” And all the congregation brought him without the camp and stoned him, as the Lord commanded Moses.

That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. There was no offering for him, the way there was a kid of the goats for the ruler who sinned through ignorance.

precepts.text: The children of Israel are commanded to make fringes in the borders of their garments to remember and do the commandments.
precepts.point: Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, who carried Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity unto this day.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

precepts.why:
“Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue”. The fringes were given so that we would look upon them and remember the commandments, and do them, and not go a-whoring after our own eyes.

These tribes failed to do that. “And they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God destroyed before them.” Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried away Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity “unto this day.”

points: When Israel came into the land of their habitations, they were to make an offering by fire unto the Lord: a burnt offering, a sacrifice in performing a vow, a freewill offering, or an offering in the solemn feasts, for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
These are all the accounts on which you would sacrifice to the Lord, taken of the herd or of the flock.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: Every sacrifice came with its measured meat offering of flour mingled with oil and its drink offering of wine, and the measures scaled up with the animal: a lamb, a ram, and then a bullock.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: An hin is roughly a gallon to a gallon and a half, so the bullock, the greatest offering, carried half an hin of oil and half an hin of wine.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: Thus it was done for one bullock, one ram, one lamb, or a kid; the kid is the goat. Everyone did according to the number they prepared.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: All that are born of the country did these things after this manner when offering an offering made by fire of a sweet savour unto the Lord.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: One ordinance and one law stood both for the congregation and for the stranger that was joined with them, an ordinance for ever in their generations: as ye are, so shall the stranger be before the Lord.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: The scripture separates the two: the children of Israel and the stranger that sojourns with them. If a stranger joined himself to Israel, he had to keep the law to journey with them in the land.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: The heave offering was a particular motion in presenting it: the offering was held up to the Most High and brought back down; that is why it was called the heave offering.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: When Israel ate of the bread of the land, they offered up a cake of the first of their dough as an heave offering unto the Lord, as they did the heave offering of the threshingfloor.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: If the whole congregation sinned through ignorance, without the knowledge of what they were doing, and the priest came behind them and corrected them on it, then all the congregation offered a young bullock for a burnt offering and a kid of the goats for a sin offering.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: The priest made an atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it was forgiven them, for it was ignorance; the stranger among them was included in that forgiveness.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: If any single soul sinned through ignorance, he brought a she goat of the first year for a sin offering, and the priest made an atonement for him, and it was forgiven him.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: One law covered him that sinned through ignorance, both for him born among the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourned among them.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: But the soul that doeth ought presumptuously sinned willfully; he thought about what he was doing before he did it. Whether born in the land or a stranger, that soul reproached the Lord and was cut off from among his people.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: Because he despised the word of the Lord and broke his commandment, that soul was utterly cut off, meaning put to death, and his iniquity was upon him.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: The man found gathering sticks on the sabbath day is the example of the presumptuous sin just described: someone who thought about the sin before he did it. He was not picking up sticks just to pick up sticks; he was gathering them to kindle a fire and cook on the sabbath.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: They put him in ward, meaning they locked him up, because it was not declared what should be done to him; then the Lord commanded Moses that the man be surely put to death, and all the congregation stoned him with stones without the camp.
He did not even get to the act itself; he had the intention, and for that willful intent he was put to death.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: Because of that act, the Most High gave Israel the commandment to make fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and to put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: The fringe is to look upon and remember all the commandments of the Lord and do them, and not to seek after your own heart and your own eyes; so that when we think of sin, we look at the fringes and remember the laws of the Most High instead of going and picking up sticks.

note.label: Numbers 15: Offerings, Presumptuous Sin, and the Fringes

points: I am the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God.
